text:
Maya: heads up	new int8 bring-up showing MRR@10 down ~6% while NDCG@10 is unchanged. suspect top1 reorder due to token boundary shifts.
Dev: numbers?
Maya: baseline float MRR=0.498, int8 MRR=0.468, NDCG@10 float=0.703, int8=0.703. harness run id run/2026-04-10/03
Noor: did we change any candidate truncation or the separator used when concatenating title+snippet? even a different separator (" - ") can change token splits.
Maya: yep last week we switched from " - " to " \u2014 " (emdash) to reduce ambiguity in UI. sample candidate: "Install99 package  \u2014 instructions"
Carlos: emdash and some control chars can create extra tokens. quant kernels sometimes handle those small-token logits differently, pushing a different item to top1 (MRR) without changing NDCG much.
Noor: quick local ablation? strip control chars, replace emdash with ascii hyphen, and try per_channel quant.
Maya: PTQ config for this build: `quant_mode=int8_static, per_channel=false, calib_samples=4096, seed=11`
Dev: run matrix: A) baseline serializer + per_channel=true, B) normalized serializer (NFKC + control-char-strip) + per_channel=false, C) both fixes. small 2k probe results: A: MRR=0.483, B: MRR=0.491, C: MRR=0.500 (beats float slightly)
Maya: that suggests both items matter but serializer normalization is larger. I'll push a bench diff and start a 10k shadowbench A/B.
bench-bot: shadowbench queued: sb-900 est 2h -> /ops/bench/sb-900/logs
Noor: also add a CI unit test that injects emdash vs hyphen and asserts no >1% MRR regression in rerank-smoke.
Maya: PR opened #812: adds NFKC+control-char-strip, reverts to ascii hyphen for concat, and adds unit + bench regen.
bench-bot: sb-900 complete: patched vs baseline: NDCG@10 +0.1%, MRR@10 +4.9% (patched wins)
Carlos: ok to merge once eng perf signs off. also note for docs: when serializing candidate text, avoid exotic punctuation or normalise to ascii where possible.
Maya: thanks team, closing loop unless someone sees a counterexample.
